rationale:
Issue #6 reports incorrect `v` value (1 instead of 0) in Ethereum signatures, causing signature endings to differ (1c vs 1b). The minimized production patch adds exactly one behavior change: `v ^= 1` inside the existing low-s canonicalization branch (`if (s > (priv.curve.n >> 1))`). This flips the recovery id when s is normalized, which is the correct Ethereum signature behavior per the cited stackexchange reference. The accompanying `(y % BigInt.two)` → `(y & BigInt.one)` change is semantically equivalent for non-negative y values. The trigger test added in the same commit uses only pre-existing APIs (ethereumSign, getV, getEIP155V, EthSignature.fromRSV, toEthCompactHex) with deterministic fixtures to assert the expected v values (27/37). Strict runtime validation confirms the trigger fails on buggy (expects v=27, gets v=28) and passes on fixed across 3 repetitions with deterministic fingerprints. No active duplicate root causes exist in this project.

Issue #6 reports incorrect Ethereum signature recovery value `v` (returning 1 instead of 0, causing signature suffix to be `1c` instead of `1b`). The minimized production patch adds exactly two lines: `v ^= 1;` inside the existing low-s canonicalization branch (`if (s > (priv.curve.n >> 1))`), plus a comment citing the Ethereum Stack Exchange rationale. This correctly flips the recovery bit when `s` is normalized to its low form, which is required by ECDSA malleability prevention. The accompanying change from `y % BigInt.two` to `y & BigInt.one` is semantically equivalent for non-negative BigInt. The trigger test was added in the same commit and uses only pre-existing APIs (ethereumSign, getV, getEIP155V, EthSignature.fromRSV, toEthCompactHex), passing deterministic fixtures with specific expected R, S, v values. Strict runtime validation confirms the test fails deterministically at buggy revision 8b87d9f (reproduced across 3 repetitions) and passes at fixed revision 6d91e66. No active duplicate root causes exist in this project.
